questions.question: For the best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they don't catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen in areas where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you in one spot in the lane and limits your movement.
Lets you rely on others to find hazards.
Requires you to go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. If it is safe, change lanes and let them go ahead. Speeding up can make the danger worse.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You don't need to look over your shoulder if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can trust that drivers will respond to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Don't protect your eyes as well as eyeglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. A face shield protects your whole face. Eyeglasses are not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which affects your motorcycle's handling. Expect slower acceleration, slower turning, and longer stopping distance. Ride slowly, slow down sooner, keep more space around you, and wait for bigger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can impair your riding. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What is the main active chemical in marijuana?
questions.explanation: The main active chemical in marijuana is called THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

questions.question: Common drugs like cold medicine:

options.text: Can affect your ability to safely ride.
Usually won't affect your riding ability.
Are always safe to take before riding because they're sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to safely ride.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your riding ability. Know the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black letters. They tell drivers what rules to follow. You must obey these signs.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing helps others see you at any time. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing whenever you ride.

questions.question: Once a motorcycle helmet has been involved in a crash, it should be:
questions.explanation: Always replace a helmet after a crash. Even if it looks fine, it may be damaged inside.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because of their small size.
Have blind spots, but they are so small they should not cause concern.
Have blind spots that should be routinely checked.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that should be routinely checked.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: Clothing made of which material offers the best protection to motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely when riding.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before and explain the process.
Not bother with explaining anything since they are only a passenger and not in control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before and explain the process.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to know how to stay safe. Never assume your passenger knows what to do. Give them full instructions before every ride.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, a jacket should be worn:

options.text: Only if the ride will be longer than half an hour.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and dehydration.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all controls are before you ride.

questions.question: To get the best protection, be sure that your helmet:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and have no visible damage.

questions.question: Waiting for one hour to ride after having one drink:

options.text: Guarantees that you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Guarantees that your riding skills will not be affected.
Should be fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not entirely remove the effects of alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not entirely remove the effects of alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. But the time it takes varies by person. The safest choice is never to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes other drivers able to see you.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is a good method.
Squeeze the tire to check it.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A low tire may look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects the wearer from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from injury in a crash. It also protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown by other vehicles.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Encourage them to take quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have had too much to drink. Take their keys if needed. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: It is best to not ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
Other drivers may need to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to a vehicle in another lane is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape path if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder and stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you, even in daylight.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it is done before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. Do not pass by riding off the main road either.

questions.question: What can help reduce the risk of a head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Fit loose enough to flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some legs.

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy material that cover your entire legs. Fit should be snug enough so clothing does not flap in the wind, but loose enough to move freely.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: For maximum protection, your motorcycle helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their system?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: You have been drinking. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You will be safe if you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can build up in your system. Your judgment and riding ability can still be impaired.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be more visible to other drivers. This helps during both day and night riding.

questions.question: To stay in control while turning your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle appropriately.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make control difficult and should be avoided.
Improve your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Improve your grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen to:

options.text: Those who completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to untrained, beginning riders who don't know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
The alcohol will not affect your riding.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up and affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: If a friend wants to ride after drinking, you should:

options.text: Get other friends to talk them out of it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of it.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Stop them any way you can. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it both day and night.
